summary: An owner disputes that tipped workers were underpaid and says the rule forces cuts.
realLife: A restaurant owner said the new rule made owners raise prices, cut servers or scale back service, and that his own costs rose about thirty thousand dollars a year even with a service charge in place. He called the idea that servers were underpaid a false story. A trade group head said owners must make up any shortfall, while advocates said some did not.
